name: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
question: Does the critical-line assertion hold for every Dirichlet L-function?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
dispatch_next: Reproduce a published primitive character modulo 3 or 5 with the correct root number, branch conventions and independently checked zero count; document why this is known mathematics, not GRH progress.
dispatch_why: The new engine verifies χ4 only; the generalized Riemann hypothesis concerns all Dirichlet characters. Replaying a separate primitive-character certificate tests the reusable contour and gamma-factor implementation.

campaign.method: Interval-arithmetic argument counts for the real characters modulo 3, 4 and 5
campaign.hypothesis: Every non-trivial zero of every Dirichlet L-function has real part 1/2.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Extend the phase to a complex character modulo 5, where the root number is not real and the completed Lambda is no longer real on the critical line.
campaign.next_experiment: Extend the phase to a complex character modulo 5, where the root number is not real and the completed Lambda is no longer real on the critical line.
campaign.falsification: A primitive character and a height T at which the certified argument count exceeds the number of critical-line sign changes.
campaign.blocker: Three real characters at height at most 17 do not constrain complex characters or large conductors.

probes.name: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
probes.title: Critical-line zero counts for the real characters modulo 3, 4 and 5
probes.frontier: Known: zeros of Dirichlet L-functions have been tabulated far beyond these heights. The certificate covers three real primitive characters only. Reproduction only, and not a proof of GRH.

smoke.scope: Critical-line certificates for χ₄ on (0, 11] with N(11) = 2; χ₃ on (0, 9] with N(9) = 1. Each argument count equals the number of disjoint intervals where that character's real Z-function changes sign, so every non-trivial zero in those ranges is simple and on the critical line.

deep.scope: Critical-line certificates for χ₄ on (0, 17] with N(17) = 4; χ₃ on (0, 15] with N(15) = 2; χ₅ (Legendre symbol mod 5) on (0, 12] with N(12) = 3. Each argument count equals the number of disjoint intervals where that character's real Z-function changes sign, so every non-trivial zero in those ranges is simple and on the critical line.

milestones.title: Low zeros of L(s, chi_4) and L(s, chi_3) are simple and on the critical line
milestones.scope: Two real characters at classical heights; not the generalized Riemann hypothesis
milestones.description: Argument counts matched to sign changes: chi_4 on (6, 7) and (10, 11) gives N(11) = 2, and chi_3 on (8, 9) gives N(9) = 1. Gauss sums tau(chi_3)^2 = -3 and tau(chi_4) = 2i fix the root numbers. The deep run adds chi_4 to N(17) = 4, chi_3 to N(15) = 2, and the Legendre symbol mod 5 to N(12) = 3, with tau(chi_5)^2 = 5.
